greek.forms: Singular: μνήμη, μνήμης, μνήμῃ, μνήμην, μνήμη. Plural: μνῆμαι, μνημῶν, μνήμαις, μνήμας
greek.etymology: Root: *men- (to think, remember). English descendants: Mnemonic (memory aid device), Amnesia (loss of memory), Anamnesis (recollection, medical history), Mnemosyne (Greek goddess of memory). The root appears in Germanic *muniz > English 'mind' and Latin memoria > 'memory'
greek.usage_example: πρῶτοι δὲ καὶ τόδε Αἰγύπτιοι εἰσὶ οἱ εἰπόντες λόγον τόνδε, ὡς ἀνθρώπου ψυχὴ ἀθάνατός ἐστι — The Egyptians were first to say this, that the human soul is immortal
greek.did_you_know: Greeks invented the 'method of loci' - memorizing by visualizing items in familiar places. Simonides developed this after identifying bodies at a banquet hall collapse by remembering where guests sat. This technique is still used by memory champions today.
